jobs.title: Senior Business Operations Manager - CBO Office
jobs.description: Business Operations at Booking.com bridges strategy and execution, ensuring the organization can effectively translate priorities into outcomes. Through planning, operational governance, performance monitoring, and cross-functional coordination, we drive alignment, operational readiness, and execution excellence—helping Booking.com deliver on its Mission, Vision, and Strategy with the customer at the center. The Chief Business Officer (CBO) Office is responsible for leading business planning and operations, program management and change management for Booking.com. The CBO Office reports to Booking's Chief Business Officer and works directly with the most senior leadership across the organization, including Department LT's and corporate functions (HR/People, Finance, Legal, and Global Strategy & Development), to enable Booking.com to achieve its strategic and operational goals. The Senior Business Operations Manager serves as a strategic and hands-on operating partner to (also reporting into) the Director of Business Operations, in the CBO Office. In this high-impact role, you act as the "connective tissue" between strategy and execution for Booking.com — ensuring the company operates efficiently, scales effectively, and makes decisions grounded in data. You are responsible for shaping, building and scaling key elements of the enterprise operating system, orchestrating the translation of strategy into execution so both remain tightly aligned. The role requires strong versatility, contributing across a wide range of initiatives and adding value wherever it is most needed. Key Job Responsibilities and Duties: (Quarterly) Operational Planning & Adaptive Execution: Design, operate, and continuously improve rolling quarterly planning and execution cycles at scale that translate annual direction into near-term priorities, commitments, sequencing, and decisions. Partner closely with annual planning owners to keep the two horizons connected, using execution insights to validate assumptions, surface dependencies and trade-offs, and adjust course as conditions change. Evolve quarterly planning from a periodic event into an effective operating rhythm that improves execution velocity, agility and predictability. Strategic Portfolio, Capacity & Trade-off Management: Build and continuously improve strategic portfolio-management and capacity/resource-management practices that enable active enterprise steering. Create visibility across priorities, demand, dependencies, investment, and capacity; establish effective prioritization and decision rights; and equip leaders to make explicit trade-offs on what to start, protect, pause, re-sequence, or stop. Partner with Finance, HR and other relevant functions where needed to strengthen resource, workforce, and investment decisions. Enterprise Operating Maturity: Shape and advance operating-model improvements across the organization in line with leadership direction and sponsorship. Translate emerging strategic direction into practical improvements to quarterly governance, leadership rhythms, decision-making, standards, and ways of working. Build alignment across senior stakeholders; pressure-test approaches against operational realities, and pilot, test, and scale improvements where there is organizational mandate. Progressively mature the operating model as priorities, permissions, and organizational readiness evolve. Data-Driven Insights & Performance Monitoring: Synthesize qualitative and quantitative data into actionable insights and executive-ready materials (dashboards, presentations, and reviews) to support leadership decision-making. Proactively monitor operational realities to surface risks and opportunities, providing data-backed recommendations for timely course correction. Cross-Functional Leadership & Initiatives: Act as a central connector across internal teams and departments (e.g., Product, Strategy, Finance, HR) to align and translate (strategic) priorities into actionable work. Lead and deliver high-visibility, cross-functional initiatives end-to-end—from scoping and stakeholder alignment to execution and impact measurement—ensuring blockers are resolved and intended outcomes are achieved. Process Improvements: Partners with senior leadership and operational teams to scope internal improvement opportunities, pressure-test proposed approaches against on-the-ground realities, and support trade-off discussions, in order to ensure internal decisions are both strategically sound and practically executable. Leadership Support & Governance: Prepares, facilitates, and follows up on internal leadership forums, offsites, and strategic reviews as needed — ensuring outcomes, owners, and timelines are clearly defined and cascaded to operational teams — in order to close the loop between strategic discussion and ground-level execution. Craft Maturity: Actively contributes to advancing the Business Operations craft at Booking.com by bringing in and applying external best practices and expertise to strengthen the function. Resource Planning: May partner with Finance and HR to manage headcount tracking, workforce planning, and budget allocation across the CBO scope to ensure resource decisions are sound, variances are flagged early, and corrective actions are taken promptly. Note: This role does not have ownership of Booking.com strategic direction or priority-setting, and does not define, manage or report on P&Ls or company-level strategy. But you may have the opportunity to influence how strategy is translated, structured, and executed, which can shape outcomes. It is also not a traditional operations role solely focused on driving measurable efficiencies in company-wide systems/workflows or in volume-based functions (e.g., customer service). Role Qualifications and Requirements: Bachelor degree required Master degree (preferred) in Business or a related field. Extensive Knowledge; 8+ years of experience in strategy, business operations, strategic program management, or a similar strategic/operational function at a fast-paced, complex organization. (Note: Solid experience working and executing initiatives within a company; consultancy experience only will not be considered). Required: Quarterly Operational Planning & Adaptive Execution: Demonstrated experience designing and maturing quarterly or similarly adaptive planning and execution practices at scale, connecting annual direction to near-term commitments, sequencing, trade-offs, and course correction. Strategic Portfolio, Capacity & Trade-off Management: Demonstrated experience improving portfolio and capacity/resource-management practices, creating visibility across priorities, demand, dependencies, investment, and resources, and enabling effective prioritization and reallocation decisions at scale. Enterprise Operating Maturity: Experience shaping and implementing operating-model improvements across complex organizations, including governance, leadership rhythms, decision rights, standards, and ways of working. Able to move from concept to practical implementation while building senior stakeholder alignment. Digital Product & Technology Environment: Strong experience operating in a large-scale, complex digital organization, with exposure to customer-facing product and technology teams and a solid understanding of product operating models, development lifecycles, cross-functional delivery, and outcome-oriented ways of working. Strategic Problem Solving & Analytical Acumen: Strong ability to connect strategy, operational realities, and data; break down complex and ambiguous problems; synthesize quantitative and qualitative insights; and translate them into clear recommendations and actions. Sound financial acumen, including understanding key business and P&L drivers. Cross-Functional Leadership & Senior Stakeholder Influence: Proven ability to operate across Product & Tech, Strategy, Finance, HR, and other functions, influence VP/SVP-level stakeholders without direct authority, build alignment across competing perspectives, and drive decisions and follow-through. Complex Initiative & Change Delivery: Experience leading complex, cross-functional Business Operations, operating-model, or organizational initiatives end-to-end, including scoping, governance, stakeholder alignment, dependency and risk management, implementation, and adoption. Strong communication skills and ability to produce executive-ready materials. Technology, Data & Work Management Tools: Experience using modern planning, work-management, and collaboration tools such as Jira/Atlassian, with a strong interest in using AI, automation, and data to improve planning, decision-making, execution visibility, and operational effectiveness. Preferred: Operating in a large-scale, complex digital organization of 8,000+ employees, experience in a B2C technology, platform, or marketplace company. Familiarity with enterprise financial planning tools and business intelligence platforms (e.g., Tableau, Anaplan). Fluency in SQL or experience working closely with data/analytics teams. Prior experience in a Chief of Staff, Business Operations, or Strategy & Operations capacity within a large, global organization. Your Traits: Independently manages multiple complex projects/programs from start to finish, with deadlines. Structured and strategic thinker who thrives in complexity and ambiguity. Obsessively data-driven; you balance qualitative insights while trusting numbers over opinions. Energized by technology and AI—actively explores how emerging tools can make the business smarter, faster, and more effective. A natural connector who brings the right people together. High bar of excellence, and equally at home in the big picture and the details (strategically minded, yet execution-focused). Calm and resilient under pressure, able to manage competing priorities and adapt quickly in fast-moving environments. A clear and persuasive communicator who presents with impact and adapts style effectively to suit any audience. Your Operating Style: Simplifier: You simplify the complex and make the implicit explicit. Influencer: You have the ability to lead through influence, effectively aligning stakeholders at all levels (including VPs/SVPs), even in the face of competing priorities. Biased for Action: You are biased toward action but measured in judgment. Possesses the intellectual curiosity of a consultant and the grit of an operator. Trusted Partner: You build trust quickly, maintain it over time, and default to collaboration rather than silos. Highly Organized: You make sure all processes/projects/programs run smoothly and reliably, designing effective tools and resources to drive optimization and meet internal partners' expectations. jobs.title: Risk & Compliance Officer- AI Risk
jobs.description: About the team: Booking.com follows a defense in depth strategy for managing its risks. As part of this strategy, Booking has 3 departments focusing on each line of defense. Global Internal Audit (GIA) is responsible for the 3rd line of defense, Risk and Controls (R&C) is responsible for the 2nd line of defense, while the responsibility of the 1st line has been distributed between process/control owners and the Tech Risk Operations (TRO) team. TRO is the first-line risk team responsible for Central Tech business unit risks and Security, Safety & Fraud (SS&F) risks across the company. About the role: The AI Risk & Compliance Officer is a senior individual contributor in the TRO Risk Management team. The role will help Booking.com identify, assess, treat, monitor, and report AI and GenAI risks across the AI lifecycle. The role will translate risk appetite, internal standards, regulatory expectations, and recognised frameworks into practical requirements that teams can apply when designing, procuring, deploying, changing, and operating AI systems. The role will operate across business and technology environments. It will partner closely with AI and Data Governance, Security, Legal, Regulatory Compliance, engineering teams,, and internal and external assurance stakeholders.. The successful candidate will be able to understand AI and cyber security architecture at a level sufficient to identify material risk, challenge control design, and support proportionate, actionable risk decisions. The role is expected to strengthen the connection between policy and execution by making AI risk decisions traceable, measurable, and embedded into existing risk management, intake, issue management, control, and assurance processes. Key Responsibilities and Duties: Responsibility 1. Risk and Compliance Partnership Act as a Risk Partner to platform owners and development teams, providing expertise in NIST, EU AI Act, NIS2 and security best practices and tailoring compliance requirements to AI systems deployment. Architect "Guardrails" for secure and compliant AI systems development, ensuring that security is "baked in" rather than "bolted on." Provide Right-Sized Advisory on control design. You will champion agile and scalable solutions that solve problems without overengineering, ensuring controls are effective but not obstructive. Bridge the Gap between technical teams and audit functions, translating complex tech stacks into risk-based language for Internal/External Audit. 2. Risk Assessments Lead or perform risk assessments for new AI initiatives, material changes, new providers, high-impact use cases, and AI systems requiring enhanced review. Evaluate security and control implications of model access, data flows, prompt and input handling, tool permissions, external integrations, model outputs, human oversight, and fallback mechanisms. Provide clear, risk-based conclusions and pre-launch conditions, including required mitigations, monitoring, ownership, escalation paths, and residual-risk decisions. Maintain the AI Risk Inventory. Systematically track and monitor identified issues originating from audits, penetration tests, and risk assessments to ensure Booking.com maintains a robust and resilient risk posture against current and emerging attack vectors. Develop and monitor AI risk indicators and metrics, including measures related to shadow AI, assessment coverage, control implementation, vulnerability remediation, AI inventory completeness, agent and tool access, monitoring coverage, incidents, and overdue actions. Analyse trends, recurring findings, control weaknesses, and changes in the threat or regulatory environment to identify systemic risk and prioritise treatment. Support risk owners in selecting and documenting appropriate treatment options, including mitigation, avoidance, transfer, or acceptance in line with risk appetite. Follow up on remediation plans and ensure that out-of-appetite risks, overdue actions, and significant control gaps are escalated through the appropriate TRO and security governance forums. Perform root-cause analysis on AI-related findings and recommend structural improvements rather than isolated corrective actions. 3. Automation & Continuous Improvement Drive Automation Initiatives by identifying manual compliance bottlenecks and designing efficient workflows leveraging automation and AI. Unify Control Frameworks across various platforms to simplify compliance and reduce "compliance fatigue" for engineering teams. Enhance Methodology: Contribute to refinement of risk assessment procedures to keep pace with the dynamic nature of a high-growth tech environment. Contribute to the evolution of Booking.com’s AI risk management framework, including the AI risk taxonomy, risk statements, control requirements, assessment methodology, risk appetite measures, and reporting model. Identify opportunities to automate risk assessments, evidence collection, control monitoring, issue tracking, and management reporting. 4. Risk Reporting & Compliance Execution Deliver Data-Driven Risk Insights by reporting on risk coverage and issues using tools like Jira and ServiceNow. Coordinate responses to internal and external assurance activities, including evidence requests, walkthroughs, control testing, maturity assessments, and follow-up of findings. Support readiness for EU AI Act requirements and other applicable AI, cyber security, data, technology, and digital-resilience obligations. Qualifications and Skills: Demonstrated experience assessing and managing risks in complex technology environments, preferably involving AI, machine learning, generative AI, cloud platforms, software engineering, or data-intensive products. Strong understanding of AI and GenAI risks across the lifecycle, including data, model, application, human, operational, cyber security, third-party, regulatory, privacy, safety, reliability, and responsible-use risks. Working knowledge of AI governance and risk frameworks, especially NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act requirements, ISO/IEC 42001, and relevant cyber security frameworks. Familiarity with AI-specific security risks and mitigations, including prompt injection, model or data poisoning, sensitive-data leakage, insecure tool use, excessive agency, supply-chain risks, and insufficient monitoring. Technical understanding of internal control requirements and design and experience in applying them in various businesses. About the FP&A internship programme Move beyond compiling data and help tell the story behind the numbers. This internship offers the opportunity to learn about ways of working at Booking.com, apply the theory learnt from the books into real life work, strengthen analytical skills that drive business insights to drive actions & decision making as well as learning/improving key skills that are critical for Finance professionals. A great opportunity to understand financial forecasting, business partnering and the modern financial planning technology stack, that powers the decision-making of a market-leader in the international travel space. You will also be part of and work on specific projects and support the daily operations of the different teams in the Finance organizations. An ideal opportunity for someone with a solutionist attitude who is curious about learning and who wants to be part of a high performing and agile team, based in the modern, central Booking.com headquarters in the heart of Amsterdam. As a Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) Intern you will be responsible for: Assist with business planning, financial forecasting, budgeting, and variance analysis to support data-driven decision making; Support the creation of scalable, insightful reporting and dashboards on key financial and business metrics; Partner with business/or and accounting teams during month-end close to accurately report results, including variance and explanatory commentary; Perform ad-hoc analysis, scenario modeling, and benchmarking, and contribute to new business, expansion, cost-control, or process-improvement projects as needed; Contribute to FP&A transformation initiatives, spanning both reporting/process improvements and the planning systems and tools that enable them; For the students with strong foundation (or interest) in technical skills, some intern positions will focus on co-creating digital reports, financial forecasting tools (such as Anaplan) and predictive forecasting Machine Learning models. Bring your sense of adventure and the following: Enrolled in a Masters or Bachelor’ degree in Business, Finance, Accounting or other related field; Advanced knowledge of Excel/Google Sheet, Powerpoint/Google-slide; Excellent communication skills; A critical mindset and a strong desire to aid in data-driven decision making; Affinity with technology, in particular AI tooling are highly preferred; Proactive Attitude: a team player and self-starter who also has the ability to work independently; Comfortable working in cross-functional teams and in a multicultural environment The following are a plus: Foundational knowledge of Python, SQL, statistical modelling, and data mining Some experience with financial modelling, planning/EPM tools (e.g., Anaplan), data warehousing tools (e.g., Snowflake), and data/process automation We are open for students who are in their 2nd/3rd/last year of their study to apply for our internship opportunity. For the students in their last year of study, we can support their graduation thesis during the internship (with alignments prior to the start of the internship). In order to be eligible for this programme you need to: Be enrolled in a Dutch University in a Bachelor or a Master for the entire length of the internship Be able to commit to attending our in-person final interview day (Assessment Centre) on November 27th, 2026 in our Amsterdam HQ. Be available for a minimum 32hrs (to 40 hours per week) paid internship from February 1st 2027, till end of July 2027 (6 months). Be able to commute to our office in Amsterdam at least twice a week throughout the internship.
